elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: 14.1(A)(1) requires CGL "with primary limits of not less than two million dollars ($2,000,000)" but states no basis; the clause does not say the limit is per occurrence, so the per-occurrence basis cannot be confirmed from the operative text.

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: No aggregate limit is expressed anywhere in 14.1(A)(1); only an unqualified "primary limits" figure of $2,000,000 appears, and the redline does not add an aggregate.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: The inserted sentence sets Professional Liability (Errors and Omissions) at "not less than one million dollars ($1,000,000)", below the preferred USD 2,000,000.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted Cyber and Privacy Liability limit is "not less than two million dollars ($2,000,000)", below the preferred USD 5,000,000 for a vendor processing Customer Data.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: Retained 14.1(A)(3): "Workers' Compensation Insurance as mandated or allowed by the state in which the Services are being performed, including at least five hundred thousand dollars ($500,000) coverage for Employer's Liability."

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: Retained 14.1(B): "annually thereafter, at Customer's request, M&I shall deliver to Customer original Certificates of Insurance evidencing the coverage required by this Section" — which now captures the new E&O and cyber policies.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted into the 14.1(A) schedule: "Professional Liability (Errors and Omissions) Insurance in an amount not less than one million dollars ($1,000,000)", carried by the "at its own cost and expense" lead-in for the Term.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Cyber and Privacy Liability Insurance in an amount not less than two million dollars ($2,000,000)", with no narrowing to selected data categories.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: the single inserted item supplies E&O at USD 1,000,000 and cyber/privacy at USD 2,000,000, and both attach to the retained 14.1(A) lead-in ("Throughout the Term ... at its own cost and expense") and the 14.1(B) certificate/notice mechanics, which expressly cover "the coverage required by this Section".

Preferred level is not complete: no aggregate CGL limit exists, the CGL basis (per occurrence) is unstated, E&O is USD 1M rather than USD 2M, and cyber is USD 2M rather than USD 5M. To reach preferred, the drafter would need to restate 14.1(A)(1) as "not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate" and raise the inserted limits to USD 2,000,000 (E&O) and USD 5,000,000 (cyber/privacy).

Minimality holds: nothing is deleted, existing favourable terms (fidelity USD 10M, workers' compensation, all-risk property, "A"-rated carriers, 30 days' notice, annual certificates) are retained, and no extras are added — no separate survival tail, no duplicated at-own-expense or certificate language, no added procedures.

Intent preserved: no undefined terms, no dangling cross-references, and no retained sentence contradicts the new coverages; 14.1(B) applies to them by its own "coverage required by this Section" wording.
Drafting nit only (not a defect in substance): the new item is appended without a list number in a numbered schedule — label it "5." so the schedule reads consistently.

Classification as a deviation is supportable notwithstanding the existing insurance clause, because the clause failed both fallback elements (no E&O, no cyber) for a vendor processing Customer Data; severity remains low.
